# Training and serving capability matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/gates/training-capabilities.py from scripts/gates/training-capabilities.tsv; edit the declaration, not this page. -->

Which architecture can be fine-tuned how, over which checkpoint precision,
and served with adapters and which KV tiers. Every cell names the test that
backs it; a cell with no test is written `-` and means "not offered", never
"untested but probably works". Per-model pages hold the commands. This page
does not record speed or memory figures.

Tests are named `crate/tests/file.rs::test_name` (or `crate/src/file.rs` for a
unit test). A test that needs a real checkpoint or a CUDA card is marked
`(real)` or `(cuda)`; the others run on the CPU backend with random weights.
`gpt2` trains from scratch (see its page) and offers no adapter.

none stores trainable parameters or optimizer moments below fp32.

## Checkpoint precision on load

| Source | What stays packed | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Q8_0 GGUF into int8 weights | the blocks are repacked, never expanded to fp32 | `flux2/tests/gguf_direct_int8.rs::gguf_int8_is_bit_identical_to_the_fp32_round_trip`, `model/src/int8.rs` |
| brain packed-int8 safetensors | words copied as stored | `checkpoint/src/weightio.rs::with_tensor_u32_chunks_is_memory_bounded` |
| FP8 HF directory into bf16 or NF4 base | nothing: each tensor is dequantized to fp32 on the host, one tensor at a time, then packed; a one-off bounded conversion into a packed file (convert_to_file) lets every later load preserve the NF4 bytes | `qwen35/tests/fp8_source.rs::streaming_the_whole_model_keeps_host_allocation_near_one_tensor`, `qwen35/tests/convert_base.rs::a_base_converted_once_equals_the_base_converted_on_every_load` |
| Other GGUF quant types (Q4_K and the rest) | nothing: decoded to fp32 and requantized to the requested tier; the packed relayout is tested but no loader uses it | `gguf/tests/kquant.rs` |

A LoRA adapter trains over an FP8 base on qwen3 and qwen35. NVFP4 and MX
checkpoints have `Weight` storage and execution but no model's LoRA trainer
offers them as a base yet. The contributor roadmap for these gaps is
`.agents/roadmap/quantized-training.md`.
